summary: Round 2 re-review of all 8 units. The revised MHA/MCA material is now accurate and consistent across the lesson text, worked example, summary bullet, comparison table and q010 (stem, marking guide, explanation): s63 covers treatment of the disorder including its symptoms and consequences (B v Croydon 1995, Nottinghamshire v RC 2014), unrelated physical illness goes to the MCA, an informal patient's refusal is judged under the MCA, and the s2/s3/s5(2)/s136 (24h, +12h)/s135/s17 details are correct. q010 has a single defensible marking guide. The DVLA wording and the valproate pregnancy-prevention caveat are now correct. All 22 numeric keys were recomputed and are correct (alcohol units 30.5/69.3/7.92, PHQ-9 45%, GAD-7 9/16, lithium rise 0.9, BMI 32.0/16.2/15.6, Bazett 465/492, corrected calcium 2.65/2.90, 4AT 7, AUDIT-C 7/10, EPDS 14/8). No control characters, tabs, literal \uXXXX text, placeholder steps or garbled characters were found. Only minor issues remain. This is an AI review; the course still needs a subject-matter expert (psychiatrist and mental health law specialist) before clinical or legal reliance.

issues.problem: The explanation says 'the MHA covers treatment of mental disorder, not physical treatment, so the refusal stands'. This is broader than the revised lesson, which teaches that s63 can cover physical consequences of the mental disorder (including self-harm injuries) in a detained patient. The key is still correct because the patient is not detained.
issues.suggestedFix: Reword to: 'He is not detained, so the MHA gives no power to treat him; the refusal is judged under the MCA, where capacity is presumed and an unwise decision is not incapacity.'

issues.problem: 'treatment ... can be given without consent to a detained patient' under s63 is stated generally. Part 4 (including s63) does not apply to patients held under s5(2), s4, s135 or s136, and ECT and some treatments have separate safeguards (s58, s58A). The scope could mislead a student who reads 'detained' as any holding power.
issues.suggestedFix: Add a short qualifier such as 'a patient detained for assessment or treatment under s2 or s3 (not those held only under s5(2), s135 or s136)', and note that ECT and some treatments have separate safeguards.

issues.problem: 'Mental health law is under reform (the Mental Health Bill), and Deprivation of Liberty Safeguards are due to be replaced by Liberty Protection Safeguards' may be out of date, because reform status and LPS plans have changed since these statements were written. This could not be verified here. The hedge 'check the current status' is present.
issues.suggestedFix: Verify current status (whether the Mental Health Bill has been enacted and commenced, and the current position on LPS) and update the sentence, or reword to a neutral 'recent and planned reforms to the MHA and to DoLS; check current law'.

issues.problem: The valproate pregnancy-prevention sentence sits in the perinatal depression paragraph introduced by 'For example', which may suggest valproate is a depression treatment. Lithium in pregnancy, which q010 also touches ('Drugs in pregnancy ... review'), is not mentioned.
issues.suggestedFix: Introduce it as an example of a drug needing pregnancy-risk review in women with bipolar disorder (for example valproate, with lithium also needing specialist review), or move it next to the puerperal psychosis and bipolar paragraph.

issues.problem: Carried over from round 1. The objective 'monitoring of their adverse effects' is covered for clozapine only as 'mandatory blood monitoring for neutropenia and agranulocytosis', with no thresholds or frequency. Nothing stated is wrong.
issues.suggestedFix: Either add the UK clozapine monitoring bands and frequencies with a 'check current SmPC/BNF' hedge, or state that numeric thresholds are out of scope at this year level.
